title: Perfect affine objects have pseudo-coherent finite-Tor module preimages
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. There exist an affine derived equivalence $e:D(A)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and an object $C\in D(A)$ such that $C$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], $C$ has Tor amplitude in some interval $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$ (meaning $H^i(C\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for every $A$-module $N$ and $i\notin[a,b]$), $E\cong e(C)$ in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$, and $Q\circ e$ followed by the inclusion is naturally isomorphic to termwise associated sheaf followed by $Q$. No bounded projective representative is asserted.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma perfect-lemma-perfect-affine (Tag 08EB), with More on Algebra, Definition 0656 (a perfect object of D(A) is one isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules)

proof.text: Transport the chosen over-site derived localizations to modules on open subschemes through Scheme.Modules.overEquiv, using Mathlib localization invariance under equivalence. Choose the affine equivalence e and a complex M with Q(M) isomorphic to e.inverse(E). Its comparison and counit identify S=Q(tilde(M)) with E. Transport perfectness through the over-site restriction functors. Set the output object C=Q(M).

Apply [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor] to S. Its pseudo-coherence clause transfers to Q(M) by [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion]. Apply [lem-pc-quasi-compact-finite-tor-dimension] to the local finite-Tor clause on the compact affine spectrum, obtaining a single nonempty interval.

Apply [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion] to M with this interval. The counit composed with e applied to the representing isomorphism supplies E isomorphic to e(Q(M)); retain the original natural comparison. No bounded projective replacement is constructed.
